### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **48** documentable anchor(s).

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7878cf0557737ecfde78dfa9cff7a1046a289a4a`.

⛔ **7** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7878cf0557737ecfde78dfa9cff7a1046a289a4a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `128dc2b67efce8005de5583c85cfa3b23e2663f8` — the merge of head `5d69a3251f5b34b96546b3d6b264585dbc096795` into base `7878cf0557737ecfde78dfa9cff7a1046a289a4a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 128dc2b67efce8005de5583c85cfa3b23e2663f8 && git checkout 128dc2b67efce8005de5583c85cfa3b23e2663f8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7878cf0557737ecfde78dfa9cff7a1046a289a4a 5d69a3251f5b34b96546b3d6b264585dbc096795 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7878cf0557737ecfde78dfa9cff7a1046a289a4a && git merge --no-ff 5d69a3251f5b34b96546b3d6b264585dbc096795

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7878cf0557737ecfde78dfa9cff7a1046a289a4a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7878cf0557737ecfde78dfa9cff7a1046a289a4a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6169c1ed8dbba450fb81429e6dc520bb422de872`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-update.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-validate.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/summary-batch-accumulation.ts, packages/objectql/src/summary-batch-accumulation.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/summary-rollup.test.ts, .changeset/34821-rollup-fold-followups.md, .changeset/34465-predicate-update-parent-summary-rule.md + packages/objectql/src/having-filter.ts, packages/objectql/src/no-operator-object-door.ts, packages/objectql/src/summary-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-master-detail-related.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-references-and-master-detail.ts, packages/objectql/src/declared-fields.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/objectql/src/core.ts, packages/objectql/package.json, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts, content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx (cited code and published text at this head, read, not reviewed)
Security-touching: yes

Inputs read: card #34821 body and all 8 comments (claim 7031250136, dev reports 7032185057, 7033828561, 7033989513, claim amendments 7032214252 and 7033859376); rulings 6377847361 (C, on #25477) and 6928862195 (B, on #33795); PR #35773 body, its 9 files, the net diff against merge base `0e2de25149`; the check-runs on the head and the log of Check Changeset job 136165292257; PR #34709's at-tier record 6943284591. Everything below is a reading of the tree at the head; nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

Gate verdicts at the read (60 check-runs on the head): 24 success, 22 skipped, 3 failure, 11 still in progress (Test Core 1/10 to 10/10 less one, Type Check workspace, Type Check consumer gates). The three failures are all Check Changeset. The log read (job 136165292257) fails on one line only: `.changeset/34465-predicate-update-parent-summary-rule.md exists on the merge base and was not added by this PR`, the DELIBERATE CORRECTION foreign-note refusal, as declared. The same run's ADR-0087 registration step lists `.changeset/34821-rollup-fold-followups.md [BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing] not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The test and type-check verdicts for this head do not exist yet; this record does not stand in for them.

What moves, read in the code:

- Insert door, write (`engine-insert.ts`) and preview (`engine-validate.ts`, mode insert, more than one row). Refused at head, admitted on main: a multi-row insert where some row after the first fails a rule (a validation rule one hop through a reference, or a field-level `requiredWhen` on `parent`) that reads a parent `formula` or stored computed field calculated from a `count` / `sum` / `min` / `max` roll-up the earlier admitted rows of the same batch move. Is that exactly what one-by-one refuses? For that shape, yes as far as the code reads: the delta is the admitted rows only (`accept` runs after the rules and the reference check), the first row reads the stored parent, and the calculated fields are computed by the same `loadSummaryFoldDependents` passes the predicate door uses (stored fields twice over the write image, then formulas in the read plan's order), with one image per parent carried through `advance`. The opposite direction exists too (a row main refused against the stored calculated value is admitted when earlier rows move it away from the rule's line), as one by one does; the 34821 note names only the refused direction (N1).
- Not exact, and outside the narrowing: an `avg` roll-up and a roll-up dropped mid-batch are not moved, so a calculated field over one of them keeps a stored or half-moved input (N2). A roll-up whose filter is in the nested form is now left out of the insert accumulation; on main the walker answered "no match" for that form on every new row, so the roll-up read the stored value there too and no verdict moves.
- Predicate-update door, N3: a roll-up the patch "cannot move" is no longer folded, so its rules read the stored value at every row. This is an accept-set change in BOTH directions against main, and it is declared only as value-neutral. It is value-neutral only when `summaryPatchCanMove` is right about "cannot move". It is not: see M1. Where it is right, the remaining difference from main is the stale-stored / column-scale case the card asked for.
- Preview: the multi-row insert preview now computes parent calculated fields from a SYSTEM read of the parent rows, also for the master-detail header whose columns the preview withholds per caller. See M2.
- Public surface: no schema key, error code or package-entry export moves. `attachInsertSummaryDependents`, `loadSummaryFoldDependents` (newly exported from `engine-update.ts`), `summaryPatchCanMove`, `SummaryFoldStandDown`, `SummaryFoldStandDownSink` and the two new `BatchSummaryAccumulator` members are module exports of internal files; neither `src/index.ts` nor `src/core.ts` (the two `exports` entries of `packages/objectql/package.json`) re-exports them. `ValidateHost` gains five members, internal. Right.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/objectql: patch` with a `!` title, BREAKING banner, FROM / TO and the caller's fix: the right level for a non-protocol narrowing, as on PR #34709.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: present on the PR body and the changeset, and the right arm for the insert door: no published schema or governed path moves, and an insert main admitted is refused. It does not cover M1, which moves the predicate door the other way with no declaration.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. Nothing an author can write is added, removed or re-read at authoring.
- ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: right. No key, export of a package entry, stored row or authored value changes shape; there is nothing a migration could rewrite. The marker's sentence "the value a predicate update's rule reads for a roll-up its patch cannot move" inherits M1's wording problem, not a disposition problem.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Deviation, pins in the two shared harness files and not a file named for the card: accepted by claim amendment 7032214252. Answered.
- Deviation, file-surface stop then extension to `engine-validate.ts` and the validate host in `engine.ts`: authorised by 7032214252; the host hunk in `engine.ts` is the five delegating members only. Answered.
- Deviation, `origin/main` merged in and a killed local run: no reading from the killed run is cited; the head's check-runs are the verdict. Answered.
- Deviation, the five host members on one line for the facade line ceiling: cosmetic. Answered.
- Deviation, discarded ablation spellings: not evidence on this head. Answered.
- Deviation, pushed with overlap-check exit 1 against the release PR #35129: the 34465 note is still on `main` at the read, so the correction still has a pending note to correct. If the release consumes it first, this hunk conflicts and the correction moves to the released CHANGELOG. For the seat. Answered.
- Acceptance note, N3 residual with a stale stored roll-up: accepted as the card's own ask; it holds only where the patch truly cannot move the roll-up (M1).
- Acceptance note, a descriptor dropped mid-batch keeps what `advance` carried: read and confirmed; the rule reading the roll-up itself goes back to the stored value while a calculated field keeps the half-moved image. N2.
- `open_questions`: none open; both of round one were answered by 7032214252.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5): no finding. The parent read is one `find` by `id $in` per parent object, chunked at `SUMMARY_GROUPED_AGGREGATE_CHUNK`, bounded by the distinct parents the batch's rows name, made once per batch and never per row. It is gated twice: `attachInsertSummaryDependents` returns before any read unless a rule of the batch binds a related row or header of that parent, and `loadSummaryFoldDependents` skips an object none of whose stored or formula plans reads an accumulated roll-up (the CONTROL pin counts zero parent reads). The read is the whole row, unprojected: the stored pass needs the write image and the formula pass its inputs, and no SQL expression can evaluate the formula plan. The gate is "a rule reads that parent", not "a rule reads a calculated field of it", so a rule reading only `parent.name` on a parent that has such a field pays the one read (N3). N3 of the card removes aggregates; it adds no statement.
- Transactions and concurrency: every new read happens before the batch writes, through the engine facade with the caller's context spread under `isSystem: true`, the same context shape the predicate door's dependents use, so the tenant scope is kept. Not traced into a driver. Concurrency stays unguaranteed per ruling 6377847361.

### ④ Design judgment

The insert narrowing makes the published rule real (batch equals one-by-one, ruling 6377847361 C) and takes no declared capability away. Tried against it by reading: mixed parents (deltas and images are keyed per parent object and id); a refused row mid-batch under partial mode (never accepted, moves nothing); a row whose reference check fails after the rules (not accepted); declaration order and a high-water mark (the predicate door's two-pass `written`, reused); a binding projected to the calculated field alone (the roll-up is moved from `dependents.stored`); a parent created in the same batch (only a self-referential object can do it; the related read finds no row, nothing is overlaid, unchanged from main and outside this diff). Those hold. Two things do not.

M1 (must-fix) — `summaryPatchCanMove` misses a filter field, so N3 un-folds a roll-up the patch does move, and the predicate door loses batch-equals-one-by-one where main holds it. `filterFieldNames` collects only the KEYS of the filter. `summaryOperations.filter` is the canonical `FilterConditionSchema`, which admits a `{ $field: 'other' }` comparand and an `addDays: { $field: 'n' }` offset (`filter.zod.ts`), and the fold's own walker resolves both against the row (`compareWithReference`, `having-filter.ts`). Take `late_count`, a `count` with filter `{ closed_at: { $gt: { $field: 'due_on' } } }`, a rule reading `record.project.late_count`, and a predicate update `{ due_on: … }` matching two rows. The named set is `{ closed_at }`, the patch writes none of fk / source / `closed_at`, so `summaryPatchCanMove` answers false and the descriptor never reaches the fold. On main it is folded exactly (`filterReadsThroughReference` does not screen it, the base is a database aggregate, and `contributionOf` sees each row enter or leave the filter). At head every row reads the stored value: the update admits what consecutive by-id updates refuse, the bypass #34465 closed under ruling 6928862195 (B), reopened for this shape. It is an undeclared move in the widening direction on a PR declared `narrowing`; no pin covers it (the `summaryPatchCanMove` cases name keys only); and it makes two published sentences false at this head: the 34821 note's "writes no … filter field of a roll-up" (the code's test is narrower than the sentence), and the 34465 note's "each matched row judges the summary as the rows judged before it leave it". The second is the note this PR rewrites, so the DELIBERATE CORRECTION cannot be confirmed on this head: the dropped parenthetical is rightly dropped, but another sentence of the same note stops being true here. Fix: collect the `$field` referents (the comparand and a nested `addDays`) into the named set, or answer "can move" for any condition holding one, and pin it beside the existing cases.

M2 (must-fix) — The preview now judges on header values the caller was not served. `resolvePreviewParents` keeps a header column only where the read door served this caller that very value and materialises every other declared field as `null`, with the stated line "the verdict never depends on a header value the caller could not have read in full" (`engine-master-detail-related.ts`). `patchRow` writes a computed dependent wherever `field in row`, and on a materialised header every declared field is in the row. `loadSummaryFoldDependents` computes from a SYSTEM read of the whole parent. So for a caller who can read the header but not `budget` or `remaining`, the first row of a multi-row preview reads `remaining` as `null` and every row after the first admitted one reads `budget - (moved total)` computed from the stored `budget`. The preview is inconsistent with itself across rows, and its verdict now depends on a withheld column, with caller-chosen amounts in the earlier rows to steer it. The write judges stored values by design, so the bit is not new to the platform, but the preview's per-column rule is its own and this hunk breaks it without saying so; no pin holds a withheld column. The related-binding path is a SYSTEM read on main already and is not affected. Fix in the preview door: do not lay a computed dependent (nor move a roll-up from the stored base) onto a header column the caller was not served, and pin a masked-column case; or put the question to the maintainer as a ruling before it lands.

S1 (should-fix) — `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx` is not in the diff and is stale on both doors at this head. The bulk-create paragraph still lists "a summary whose `filter` reads a dotted path" alone (the nested form now stands down too) and says nothing of calculated parent fields, which now hold; the predicate-update paragraph still says "Three cases keep reading the stored value" and "for every summary function", with no word of a roll-up the patch cannot move. PR #34709 carried the same paragraphs with its change.

N1 (nit) — The 34821 note states only the refused direction. A multi-row insert main refused against the stored calculated value can now be admitted when earlier rows move it away from the rule's line. One clause, as the 34465 note has.

N2 (nit) — A calculated field reading both an accumulated roll-up and one that stays stored (`avg`, a roll-up dropped mid-batch, a filter through a reference) is now computed over a mix of moved and stored inputs, and a roll-up dropped mid-batch leaves its half-moved value in the carried image while the roll-up itself reads stored again. The note says "computed again over the moved roll-ups" and names neither.

N3 (nit) — The parent read is gated on "a rule reads that parent", not on "reads a calculated field of it", and `foldedSummaries` is handed the rows the door already refused as well, so it can read a few parents no judged row needs. Bounded by the batch; cost only.

N4 (nit) — After this PR the 34465 note's "one grouped aggregate per summary a rule reads" and "Three cases keep reading the stored value" are exact only when read with the 34821 note beside it (a roll-up the patch cannot move is neither aggregated nor folded). Both compile into one release, so a clause in either note is enough.

The N4 debug line of the card is harmless: one `logger.debug` per roll-up stood down per update, carrying object and field names and a reason from a closed set, no row value or id.

## Seat check

**L1: ACCEPT** (L1-a, for area d7-B) at head `5d69a3251f5b34b96546b3d6b264585dbc096795`, read 2026-11-20T10:03Z. This is the first L1 on this PR.

- **One record is owed before landing, with no new head:** the `Skills-docs:` line (below).
- **One L2 is owed:** CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER on this head. The change is declared narrowing, so the L2 covers the whole non-prose diff and confirms the DELIBERATE CORRECTION. d7-B reports the same reviewer's delta L2 is running, after FAIL 7034146638. This ACCEPT does not replace it.

### Owed before landing: the `Skills-docs:` line

A `!` / `(narrowing)` PR carries a `Skills-docs:` line, and the body has none. `git grep` over `skills/` finds no sentence about a multi-row write, or a predicate update, judging a rule over a roll-up or a parent field calculated from one. So the line is `Skills-docs: none — nothing under skills/ covers how a batch insert or predicate update judges a rule over a roll-up or a calculated parent field`, or whatever reason d7-B measures. This is a body edit, with no new head and no delta L1.

### Declarations

- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` holds**, and `!` is on the title and the subject.
  - A multi-row insert now refuses a row that main admitted against the stored calculated value.
  - The changeset says honestly that it also admits the reverse case.
  - The declaration follows the predicate-update twin (PR #34709) and its rulings 6377847361 C and 6928862195 B.
- **The rest of the breaking record is there:**
  - the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`;
  - the **BREAKING** banner;
  - FROM / TO, with the concrete 3 × 40 against 100 case;
  - the fix line;
  - the full dogfood battery pinned to `5d69a325`: 482 files passed and 3 skipped; 4094 tests passed, 68 skipped, 0 failed.
  - `check-adr-0087-registration` reads it as `BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing`.

### DELIBERATE CORRECTION: `.changeset/34465-predicate-update-parent-summary-rule.md`

- **Before:** "A bulk create and a bulk update already equal one-by-one writes for a rule reading the summary itself (a bulk create does not yet for a rule reading a parent field calculated from one: its accumulator moves the summary key alone, #34821); this extends that …"
- **After:** the parenthetical is dropped, and nothing else changes.

The correction is true. This PR's accumulator calls `dependents.advance` and computes the parent's calculated fields over `movedOf` in `patchRow`, so the bulk create no longer "moves the summary key alone". The note is pending: it is still in `.changeset/` and compiles into the same release, and `Check Changeset` is red only on it (both failing runs are that job).

The diff changes code, so per landing-operations.md **the confirming record is the same-head at-tier L2 PASS**, which must name this sentence. My ACCEPT does not confirm it on its own.

**The 34465 note's aggregate sentence.** It says "one grouped aggregate per summary a rule reads". The 34821 note now qualifies it ("hold for the roll-ups the patch can move; one it cannot move is neither aggregated nor folded") rather than rewriting it. I accept that (the L2's N4). It is accurate read with the later note, and it keeps the correction to the one false parenthetical. ⛔ Nothing touches Version Packages #35129.

### Code (L1 read)

- **`summaryPatchCanMove`.** A roll-up is movable when the patch writes its FK, its `sourceField` (not for `count`), or any field its `filter` names.
  - The filter names come from keys and from `{ $field }` referents at any depth, so an `addDays` operand holding a `$field` is found by recursion.
  - An unreadable operator answers "can move", the conservative direction.
- **`movedOf` / `patchRow`.**
  - The stored image comes from `dependents.stored` when the reader was not handed the roll-up.
  - Calculated fields are written only onto columns that were served (`served(field)`).
  - In preview, `servedColumns[i]` comes from the master-detail reader's kept columns, and a null entry becomes an empty set, so a withheld column reads `null` (M2).
- **Nested-form filters** (`{ account: { status } }`) are now left out by `filterReadsThroughReference`, as the dotted form was.
- **Stand-down sink.** It reports one debug line per unfolded roll-up, with the reasons `filter`, `not_a_number` and `exclusion_budget`, as the changeset says.
- **Ablations A7–A9** red the new pins (7036621555).

### Prose, sentence by sentence

- **34821 changeset.**
  - FROM and TO match `attachInsertSummaryDependents` and the preview path.
  - "carrying the parent's stored image from row to row" matches `advance`.
  - "judges a master-detail header column the caller is not served as empty at every row" matches M2.
  - "Only a batch with a rule reading that parent pays one read of its parent rows" matches `stored`.
  - The both-ways and mixed-input bullets (N1, N2) are true by the fold.
  - The nested-form sentence and the predicate-update paragraph match `summaryPatchCanMove` and the stand-down reasons.
- **`fields.mdx`.** The calculated-field paragraph, the nested-form exception, the preview exception and the "Four cases" list (the new "a summary the patch cannot move" plus the three before) each match the code.

### Nit (not owed)

`fields.mdx`'s new case says "as a key or as a `{ $field }` comparand". The changeset adds "or `addDays` offset". The code covers both through the same recursion, so the page could name the offset too.

- After the `Skills-docs:` line and the at-tier L2 PASS on this head (naming the 34465 sentence), the SKILL.md conditions for landing red-with-correction apply, and `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35773` decides the route.
